## Full statements

### Theorem 1 (Soundness of FRJ(G))
`theo:FRJsound`  ·  p.6

$\vdash_{\mathbf{FRJ}(G)} G$ implies $G\not\in\mathrm{IPL}$. 

### Example 1
`ex:impPS1`  ·  p.8

Let $\sigma_1= \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B}$ be an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-sequent such that the formula $p\lor q\supset B$ belongs to ${\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(G)$. To apply rule $\supset_\in$ to $\sigma_1$ so to get a sequent with $p\lor q\supset B$ in the right, we have to select a subset $\Lambda$ of $\{p,q\}$ satisfying the side condition $p\lor q\in\mathcal{C}l(\Lambda)$. The following three choices are possible: $$\begin{array}{lll} \Lambda_1\;=\;\{p\} & \Lambda_2\;=\;\{q\} & \Lambda_3\;=\;\{p,q\} \\[1.5ex] \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_\in$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{q}}{\cdot}{q} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p\lor q\supset B}}{\cdot}{p\lor q\supset B} $} \DP \hspace{2em} & \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_\in$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{q}}{\cdot}{q} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p\lor q\supset B}}{\cdot}{p\lor q\supset B} $} \DP \hspace{2em} & \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_\in$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p\lor q\supset B}}{\cdot}{p\lor q\supset B} $} \DP \end{array}$$ We point out that $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are minimal sets satisfying the side condition, while $\Lambda_3$ is not. Indeed, the empty set is the only proper subset of $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ and $p\lor q\not\in\mathcal{C}l(\emptyset)$. On the other hand, $\Lambda_3$ is not minimal, since both $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are proper subsets of $\Lambda_3$. $\Diamond$

### Example 2
`ex:impPS2`  ·  p.9

Let $\sigma_1= \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B}$ be an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-sequent and let assume that $${\overline\Gamma}\;=\;{\normalfont\textsc{Sl}}(G)\cap(\mbox{$\mathcal{V}$}\cup\mathcal{L}^\supset)\;=\;\{p,\,q,\,r,\,r\supset p,\,p\supset r\} \hspace{4em} C\,=\,p\land q\supset B\,\in\,{\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(G)$$ We show all the possible applications of $\supset_{\not\in}$ to $\sigma_1$ yielding an irregular sequent of the form $\ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta}}{\cdot}{\Theta} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$. By the side conditions, $\Theta$ must be a subset of $\mathcal{C}l(\{p,q\})\cap{\overline\Gamma}=\{p,q,r\supset p\}$, which gives rise to eight possible choices: $$\begin{array}{llll} \Theta_1\,=\, \emptyset &\Theta_2\,=\,\{ p\} & \Theta_3\,=\,\{q\} &\Theta_4\,=\,\{r\supset p\} \\[.5ex] \Theta_5\,=\,\{p,r\supset p\} \qquad & \Theta_6\,=\,\{q,r\supset p\} \qquad & \Theta_7\,=\,\{p,q\} \qquad & \Theta_8\,=\,\{p,q,r\supset p\} \end{array}$$ By the side conditions, we need $p\land q\not\in\mathcal{C}l(\Theta)$, hence $\Theta_7$ and $\Theta_8$ must be ruled out. This leads to six possible applications of rule $\supset_{\not\in}$: $$\begin{array}{ll} \Theta_1\,=\,\emptyset\quad \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_{\not\in}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta_1}}{\cdot}{\Theta_1} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C} $} \DP & \Theta_2\,=\,\{ p\}\quad \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_{\not\in}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta_2}}{\cdot}{\Theta_2} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C} $} \DP \\[5ex] \Theta_3\,=\,\{q\}\quad \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_{\not\in}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta_3}}{\cdot}{\Theta_3} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C} $} \DP & \Theta_4\,=\,\{r\supset p\}\quad \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_{\not\in}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta_4}}{\cdot}{\Theta_4} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C} $} \DP \\[5ex] \Theta_5\,=\,\{p,r\supset p\}\quad \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_{\not\in}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta_5}}{\cdot}{\Theta_5} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C} $} \DP \quad & \Theta_6\,=\,\{q,r\supset p\}\quad \AXC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q}}{\cdot}{p,q} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_{\not\in}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta_6}}{\cdot}{\Theta_6} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C} $} \DP \end{array}$$ We point out that $\Theta_5$ is a maximal set satisfying the side condition. Indeed, the only proper superset $\Theta'$ of $\Theta_5$ such that $\Theta'\,\subseteq\, \mathcal{C}l(\{p,q\})\cap{\overline\Gamma}$ is $\Theta_8$ and $p\land q\in\mathcal{C}l(\Theta_8)$. Similarly, $\Theta_6$ is maximal as well. On the other hand, sets $\Theta_1,\dots,\Theta_4$ are not maximal, since each of them is a proper subset of $\Theta_5$ or $\Theta_6$. $\Diamond$

### Example 3

Let $\sigma_1= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Sigma_1 }}{\cdot}{\Sigma_1 } \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta_1}}{\cdot}{\Theta_1} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B}$, where $\Sigma_1=\{B\supset X_1, B\supset X_2, C\supset X_3 \}$ and $C\neq B$. We cannot apply a join rule having $\sigma_1$ as only premise since the formula $C\supset X_3$ would not be supported (while both $B\supset X_1$ and $B\supset X_2$ are, being $B$ the right formula of $\sigma_1$). Thus, to apply a join rule, we need a further premise $\sigma_2= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Sigma_2}}{\cdot}{\Sigma_2} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta_2}}{\cdot}{\Theta_2} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$ such that $\Sigma_1\subseteq\Sigma_2\cup\Theta_2$ and $\Sigma_2\subseteq\Sigma_1\cup\Theta_1$ (see [\[sc:J1\]](#sc:J1)). In turn, $\Sigma_2$ might contain some non-supported formulas; e.g., a formula $D\supset X_4$ such that $D\neq B$ and $D\neq C$; in this case, we need a further premise $\sigma_3$ s.t. $\mathrm{Rhs}(\sigma_3)=D$ to support it. $\Diamond$

### Lemma 1
`lemma:lhs`  ·  p.11

1. $\sigma_1\stackrel{\mathcal{R}}{\mapsto_0} \sigma_2$ and $\mathcal{R}\neq\,\supset_{\not\in}$ imply $\mathrm{Lhs}(\sigma_2)\,\subseteq\,\mathrm{Lhs}(\sigma_1)$. 2. $\sigma_1\mapsto_0\sigma_2$ implies $\mathrm{Lhs}(\sigma_2)\,\subseteq\,\mathcal{C}l(\mathrm{Lhs}(\sigma_1))$. 3. $\sigma_1\mapsto_*\sigma_2$ implies $\mathrm{Lhs}(\sigma_2)\,\subseteq\,\mathcal{C}l(\mathrm{Lhs}(\sigma_1))$. 

### Example 4
`ex:Ror`  ·  p.12

In the Introduction, by applying the unsound rule $R\lor$, we got a wrong derivation of the sequent $\sigma= \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,H}}{\cdot}{p,H} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1\lor q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1\lor q_2}$, where $H= p\supset q_1\lor q_2$. By the soundness property [\[prop:soundr\]](#prop:soundr), if $\sigma$ could be proved in $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$, there should be a world $\alpha$ of a model such that both $p$ and $H$ are forced in $\alpha$ and $q_1\lor q_2$ is not forced in $\alpha$, a contradiction. We show that it is not possible to build an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation $\mathcal{D}$ of $\sigma$. Indeed, the root rule of $\mathcal{D}$ should be $\Join^\lor$, the only rule of $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$ having as conclusion a regular sequent with an $\lor$-formula in the right. Since the formula $H$ must be supported (see [\[sc:J2\]](#sc:J2)), rule $\Join^\lor$ should have a premise $\sigma'= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Sigma'}}{\cdot}{\Sigma'} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta'}}{\cdot}{\Theta'} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p}$. Since the only irregular sequents having a formula in $\mbox{$\mathcal{V}$}^\bot$ in the right are the irregular axioms, $\mathcal{D}$ should have the following shape: $$\AXC{$\cdots$} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow$} \UIC{$\sigma'\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta'}}{\cdot}{\Theta'} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} $} \AXC{$\cdots$} \LeftLabel{$\mathcal{D}\;=\quad$} \RightLabel{$\Join^\lor$} \TIC{$\sigma\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,H}}{\cdot}{p,H} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1\lor q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1\lor q_2} $} \DP \qquad p\not\in\Theta'$$ Hence, $\sigma'\stackrel{\Join^\lor}{\mapsto_0} \sigma$ which, by Lemma [\[lemma:lhs\]](#lemma:lhs)[\[lemma:lhs:1\]](#lemma:lhs:1), implies $\{p,H\}\subseteq \Theta'$. Thus, both $p\in\Theta'$ and $p\not\in\Theta'$, a contradiction. We conclude that $\sigma$ is not provable. However, it is possible to have applications of rule $\Join^\lor$ having conclusion $\ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1\lor q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1\lor q_2}$ or $\ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1\lor q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1\lor q_2}$. For instance, let $$G\;=\; (p\land H)\,\supset\, (q_1\lor q_2) \qquad H\;= \;p\supset q_1\lor q_2$$ We have: $${\normalfont\textsc{Sl}}(G)\:=\:\{\, p\land H,\, H,\,q_1\lor q_2,\,p,\,\,q_1,\,q_2\, \} \qquad {\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(G)\:=\:\{\, G,\, \,q_1\lor q_2,\,p,\,\,q_1,\,q_2\, \}$$ We can build the following $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation: $$\begin{array}{c} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q_2,H}}{\cdot}{p,q_2,H} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1} $} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q_1,H}}{\cdot}{p,q_1,H} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} $} \RightLabel{$\Join^\lor$} \BIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1\lor q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1\lor q_2} $} \DP \end{array}$$ We point out that the side conditions [\[sc:J1\]](#sc:J1) and [\[sc:J2\]](#sc:J2) trivially hold, since the $\Sigma$-sets of the premises are empty. In the conclusion, $H$ is left out since it is not supported (no premise has $p$ in the right). Similarly, we can build the following $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation: $$\AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q_2,H}}{\cdot}{p,q_2,H} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1} $} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q_1,H}}{\cdot}{p,q_1,H} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} $} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1,q_2,H}}{\cdot}{q_1,q_2,H} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} $} \RightLabel{$\Join^\lor$} \TIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1\lor q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1\lor q_2} $} \DP$$ In the conclusion, $p$ is omitted since it does not occur as left formula in the right-most premise. We can also build the following $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation of an irregular sequent $\sigma_1$ having the goal formula $G$ in the right: $$\AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q_2,H}}{\cdot}{p,q_2,H} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1} $} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,q_1,H}}{\cdot}{p,q_1,H} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} $} \RightLabel{$\lor$} \BIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,H}}{\cdot}{p,H} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1\lor q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1\lor q_2} $} \RightLabel{$\supset_\in$} \UIC{$\sigma_1\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,H}}{\cdot}{p,H} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{(p\land H)\supset(q_1\lor q_2)}}{\cdot}{(p\land H)\supset(q_1\lor q_2)} $} \DP$$ Apparently, this contradicts the soundness of the calculus, since the formula $G$ is valid. Actually, we conclude that the hypothesis of the soundness property [\[prop:soundi\]](#prop:soundi) does not hold, namely, $\sigma_1$ cannot be used to derive in $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$ a regular sequent. $\Diamond$

### Example 5
`ex:frjNishimura`  ·  p.14

Let us consider the following instances $S$ and $T$ of *Scott* and *Anti-Scott* principles, which are equivalent to Nishimura formulas $N_{10}$ and $N_{9}$ respectively [@ChaZak:97] (the schema generating $N_i$ is given in Sec. [\[sec:rel\]](#sec:rel)): $$S\;=\;\left((\neg\neg p\supset p) \supset\neg p\lor p\right)\,\supset\,\neg\neg p \lor \neg p \qquad T\;=\; S \,\supset\,(\neg\neg p\supset p)\lor \neg\neg p$$ Both formulas are valid in Classical Logic but not in $\mathrm{IPL}$. Figs. [\[fig:frjST\]](#fig:frjST) and [\[fig:frjAST\]](#fig:frjAST) show an $\mathbf{FRJ}(S)$-derivation $\mathcal{D}_S$ of $S$ and an $\mathbf{FRJ}(T)$-derivation $\mathcal{D}_T$ of $T$ respectively, in linear representation. We populate the database of proved sequents according with the naive recipe of [@VoronkovHAR:01]: we start by inserting the axioms; then we enter a loop where, at each iteration, we apply the rules to the sequents collected in previous steps. For the sake of conciseness, we only show the sequents needed to get the goal. We denote with $\sigma_{(k)}$ the sequent derived at line $(k)$. The tree-like structure of derivations $\mathcal{D}_S$ and $\mathcal{D}_T$ are displayed in Figs. [\[fig:countST\]](#fig:countST) and [\[fig:countAST\]](#fig:countAST) respectively. We point out that $\mathcal{D}_T$ contains an application of $\Join^\lor$ having four premises, namely: $$\begin{array}{c} \AXC{$\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:2}} \qquad \sigma_{\eqref{exAST:7}} \qquad\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:8}}\qquad\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:11}}$} \RightLabel{$\Join^\lor$} \UIC{$\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:13}}$} \DP \\[3ex] \begin{array}{ll} \sigma_{\eqref{exAST:2}}\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{S,\:\neg \neg p \supset p,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p}}{\cdot}{S,\:\neg \neg p \supset p,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} \qquad & \sigma_{\eqref{exAST:7}}\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{S,\:\neg \neg p \supset p}}{\cdot}{S,\:\neg \neg p \supset p} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg\neg p} \\ \sigma_{\eqref{exAST:8}}\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{S,\:\neg \neg p \supset p,\:\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{S,\:\neg \neg p \supset p,\:\neg\neg p} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} & \sigma_{\eqref{exAST:11}}\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg \neg p \supset p}}{\cdot}{\neg \neg p \supset p} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{S,\:\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{S,\:\neg\neg p} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} \\ \sigma_{\eqref{exAST:13}}\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg \neg p \supset p,\:S}}{\cdot}{\neg \neg p \supset p,\:S} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{ \neg p\lor p }}{\cdot}{ \neg p\lor p } & S\;=\; H\,\supset\, \neg\neg p \lor \neg p \end{array} \end{array}$$ The sequent $\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:13}}$ is essential to build the countermodel since it corresponds to a world where both $\neg \neg p \supset p$ and $S$ are forced, while $\neg p\lor p$ is not; to get $\Gamma=\{ \neg \neg p \supset p,S\}$ in the left of $\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:13}}$, we have to use premises $\sigma'$ such that $\Gamma\subseteq\mathrm{Lhs}(\sigma')$ (see Lemma [\[lemma:lhs\]](#lemma:lhs)[\[lemma:lhs:1\]](#lemma:lhs:1)). Sequents $\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:8}}$ and $\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:2}}$ are needed to obtain $\neg p\lor p$ in the right of $\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:13}}$, while sequents $\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:7}}$ and $\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:11}}$ are needed to support $\neg \neg p \supset p$ and $S$ respectively. One can easily check that the side conditions [\[sc:J1\]](#sc:J1) and [\[sc:J2\]](#sc:J2) hold, thus the displayed application of rule $\Join^\lor$ is sound. Finally, we point out that it is not possible to obtain $\sigma_{\eqref{exAST:13}}$ using less than four premises. $\Diamond$

### Example 6
`ex:frjKP`  ·  p.15

Another significant example is the $\mathbf{FRJ}(K)$-derivation $\mathcal{D}_K$ of the instance $K=(\neg a \supset b\lor c)\supset(\neg a \supset b) \lor (\neg a \supset c)$ of Kreisel-Putnam principle [@ChaZak:97] shown in Fig. [\[fig:frjKP\]](#fig:frjKP). Differently from the formulas $S$ and $T$ in the previous example, the formula $K$ contains three propositional variables, which give rise to eight axioms. In the figure, we only consider the sequents needed to prove the goal. $\Diamond$

### Lemma 2
`lemma:soundFRJ`  ·  p.16

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation of $G$, let $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D})$ be the model extracted from $\mathcal{D}$ and $\phi$ the map associated with $\mathcal{D}$. For every sequent $\sigma$ occurring in $\mathcal{D}$: 1. if $\sigma= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Gamma}}{\cdot}{\Gamma} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$, then $\phi(\sigma)\Vdash\Gamma$ and $\phi(\sigma) \nVdash C$; 2. if $\sigma= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Sigma}}{\cdot}{\Sigma} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta}}{\cdot}{\Theta} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$, let $\sigma_p\in\mathrm{P}(\mathcal{D})$ such that $\sigma\mapsto\sigma_p$ and $\sigma_p\Vdash\Sigma\cap\mathrm{Sf}^-(C)$; then $\sigma_p\nVdash C$.

### Theorem 2
`theo:soundFRJ`  ·  p.17

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation of $G$. Then, $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D})$ is a countermodel for $G$.

### Example 7
`ex:count`  ·  p.17

Let us consider the formulas $S$, $T$ and $K$ in examples [\[ex:frjNishimura\]](#ex:frjNishimura) and [\[ex:frjKP\]](#ex:frjKP). The models $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D}_S)$, $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D}_T)$, $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D}_K)$ and the related maps $\phi$ are shown in Figs. [\[fig:countST\]](#fig:countST), [\[fig:countAST\]](#fig:countAST) and [\[fig:countKP\]](#fig:countKP) respectively. The bottom world is the root and $\sigma<\sigma'$ iff the world $\sigma$ is drawn below $\sigma'$. For each $\sigma$, we display the set $V(\sigma)$. As an example, in Fig. [\[fig:countST\]](#fig:countST) we have $V(\sigma_\eqref{exST:6})=\{p\}$, while $V(\sigma_\eqref{exST:5})=V(\sigma_\eqref{exST:9})=V(\sigma_\eqref{exST:11})=\emptyset$. $\Diamond$

### Lemma 3
`lemma:wg`  ·  p.19

$\sigma_1\mapsto \sigma_2$ implies $\langle 0,0,0 \rangle\preceq \mathrm{wg}(\sigma_2) \prec \mathrm{wg}(\sigma_1)$. 

### Lemma 4
`lemma:branch`  ·  p.19

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation, let $\mathcal{B}$ be a branch of $\mathcal{D}$ and $N=| G|$. Then: 1. the length of the branch $\mathcal{B}$ is $O(N^2)$; 2. $\mathcal{B}$ contains $N$ p-sequents at most.

### Theorem 3
`theo:height`  ·  p.20

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation and $N=| G|$. Then: 1. $\mathrm{h}(\mathcal{D})\,=\,O(N^2)$. 2. $\mathrm{h}(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D}))\,\leq\, N$. 

### Lemma 5
`lemma:subsRules`  ·  p.21

Let $$\AXC{$\sigma_1 \;\cdots\; \sigma_n$} \RightLabel{$\mathcal{R}$} \UIC{$\sigma$} \DP$$ be an instance of a rule of $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$ and let $\sigma_1\sqsubseteq \sigma'_1$, ..., $\sigma_n\sqsubseteq \sigma'_n$. Then, $$\AXC{$\sigma'_1 \;\cdots\; \sigma'_n$} \RightLabel{$\mathcal{R}$} \UIC{$\sigma'$} \DP$$ is an instance of $\mathcal{R}$ in $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$ where $\sigma\sqsubseteq \sigma'$.

### Theorem 4
`theo:fsearchAdequate`  ·  p.23

$\FSearch$ is an adequate proof-search procedure.

### Lemma 6
`lemma:compactSatDB`  ·  p.23

Let $G$ be a formula and let $\mathtt{D}_{G}^1$ be a compact saturated database for $G$. For every saturated database $\mathtt{D}_{G}^2$ for $G$, $\mathtt{D}_{G}^1\subseteq \mathtt{D}_{G}^2$.

### Theorem 5
`theo:uniquetSatDB`  ·  p.23

For every formula $G$, there exists a unique compact saturated database $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{G}$ for $G$, which is the minimum saturated database for $G$.

### Lemma 7
`lemma:GBUsound`  ·  p.25

If $\vdash_{\mathbf{Gbu}(G)} \tau$, then $\tau$ is valid.

### Theorem 6 (Soundness of Gbu(G))
`theo:GBUsound`  ·  p.25

$\vdash_{\mathbf{Gbu}(G)} G$ implies $G\in\mathrm{IPL}$. 

### Lemma 8
`lemma:wggbu`  ·  p.25

Let $\mathcal{R}$ be a rule of $\mathbf{Gbu}(G)$, let $\tau$ be the conclusion of $\mathcal{R}$ and $\tau'$ any of the premises of $\mathcal{R}$. Then $\langle 0,0,0 \rangle\preceq \mathrm{Wg}(\tau') \prec \mathrm{Wg}(\tau)$. 

### Theorem 7
`theo:gbufin`  ·  p.26

Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a $\mathbf{Gbu}(G)$-tree and $\tau$ the root sequent of $\mathcal{T}$. Then, the height of $\mathcal{T}$ is $O(|\tau|^2)$. 

### Example 8
`ex:gbu1`  ·  p.28

Let $E$ be the following goal formula: $$\begin{array}{l} E\;=\; (p\land A \land B \land C) \,\supset\, D \\[1ex] A\;=\; p\supset(q_1\lor q_2 ) \quad B\;=\; q_1\supset D \quad C\;=\; q_2\supset D \quad D\;=\; r_1\lor r_2 \\[1ex] \begin{array}{rcl} \mathrm{Lhs}(E)\,\cap\,(\mbox{$\mathcal{V}$}\cup\mathcal{L}^\supset) &\;=\;& \{\,p,\, q_1,\, q_2,\, r_1,\, r_2,\,A,\,B,\,C\,\} \\[1ex] \mathrm{Rhs}(E) &=& \{\,p,\, q_1,\, q_2,\, r_1,\, r_2,\,D,\,E\,\} \end{array} \end{array}$$ Since $E$ is valid and the proof-search procedure of Fig. [\[fun:FSearch\]](#fun:FSearch) is adequate (see Theorem [\[theo:fsearchAdequate\]](#theo:fsearchAdequate)), the call $\FSearch{E}$ returns a saturated database for $E$. We can exploit it to run the procedure BSearch and build a $\mathbf{Gbu}(E)$-derivation of $E$. We consider the compact saturated database $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}$ for $E$ containing the following irregular sequents $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:1}},\dots,\sigma_{\eqref{exE:6}}$ (we omit the regular sequents since they are not used by $\mbox{\sc BSearch}$): \@true $$\begin{align} \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1,\, q_2,\, r_1,\, r_2,\,A,\, B,\, C}}{\cdot}{q_1,\, q_2,\, r_1,\, r_2,\,A,\, B,\, C} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} && \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow\\ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\, q_2,\, r_1,\, r_2,\,A,\, B,\, C}}{\cdot}{p,\, q_2,\, r_1,\, r_2,\,A,\, B,\, C} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1} && \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow\\ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\, q_1,\, r_1,\, r_2,\,A,\, B,\, C}}{\cdot}{p,\, q_1,\, r_1,\, r_2,\,A,\, B,\, C} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} && \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow\\ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\, q_1,\, q_2,\, r_2,\,A,\, B,\, C}}{\cdot}{p,\, q_1,\, q_2,\, r_2,\,A,\, B,\, C} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1} && \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow\\ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\, q_1,\, q_2,\, r_1,\,A,\, B,\, C}}{\cdot}{p,\, q_1,\, q_2,\, r_1,\,A,\, B,\, C} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2} && \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow\\ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\, q_1,\, q_2,\, A,\, B,\, C}}{\cdot}{p,\, q_1,\, q_2,\, A,\, B,\, C} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} && \lor\;\eqref{exE:4} \eqref{exE:5} \end{align}$$ Proof-search starts from the sequent $\ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{E}}{\cdot}{E}$. Rules of $\mathbf{Gbu}(E)$ are backward applied according with [\[search:2\]](#search:2), until the critical sequent $\tau_1$ is obtained: $$\AXC{$\tau_1\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \doubleLine \RightLabel{$L\land$ (three times)} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p\land A\land B\land C}}{\cdot}{p\land A\land B\land C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \RightLabel{$\supset R_{\not\in}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{E}}{\cdot}{E} $} \DP \qquad \Psi_1\;=\; p,\,A,\,B,\,C$$ To continue the construction of the derivation, we have to bottom-up apply a rule of $\mathbf{Gbu}(E)$ to the critical sequent $\tau_1$, and we query $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}$ to choose the right way. We have 5 possible choices: 1. Apply rule $L\supset$ with main formula $A$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p}$. 2. Apply rule $L\supset$ with main formula $B$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1}$. 3. Apply rule $L\supset$ with main formula $C$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2}$. 4. Apply rule $R\lor_1$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1}$. 5. Apply rule $R\lor_2$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2}$. We have: $$\begin{array}{l} \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:2}}$)} \qquad \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:3}}$)} \\[1ex] \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:4}}$)} \qquad \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:5}}$)} \\[1ex] \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_1}}{\cdot}{\Psi_1} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} \end{array}$$ hence only choice [\[exE:choice1\]](#exE:choice1) can be performed. Note that, selecting any of the other options [\[exE:choice2\]](#exE:choice2)--[\[exE:choice5\]](#exE:choice5), where the corresponding condition is not matched, proof-search fails. Complying with [\[exE:choice1\]](#exE:choice1), we apply rule $L\supset$ with main formula $A$ and we continue until we get the critical sequents $\tau_2$ and $\tau_3$. $$\AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,A,\,B,\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,A,\,B,\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} $} \AXC{$\tau_2\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \AXC{$\tau_3\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_3}}{\cdot}{\Psi_3} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \RightLabel{$L\lor$} \BIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,\underline{\,q_1\lor q_2},\, B,\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,\underline{\,q_1\lor q_2},\, B,\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \RightLabel{$L\supset$} \BIC{$\tau_1\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,\underline{A},\,B,\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,\underline{A},\,B,\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \DP \qquad \begin{minipage}{10em} $\Psi_2\,=\; p,\,q_1,\,B,\,C$ \\[1ex] $\Psi_3\,=\; p,\,q_2,\,B,\,C$ \end{minipage}$$ Let us consider the critical sequent $\tau_2$. We have 4 possible choices: 1. Apply rule $L\supset$ with main formula $B$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1}$. 2. Apply rule $L\supset$ with main formula $C$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2}$. 3. Apply rule $R\lor_1$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1}$. 4. Apply rule $R\lor_2$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2}$. We note that: $$\begin{array}{l} \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:3}}$)} \qquad \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:4}}$)} \\[1ex] \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:5}}$)} \qquad \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_2}}{\cdot}{\Psi_2} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1} \end{array}$$ Thus, we choose [\[exE:choice6\]](#exE:choice6) and we continue until we get the critical sequents $\tau_4$ and $\tau_5$. $$\AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_1,\,B,\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_1,\,B,\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1} $} \AXC{$\tau_4\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_4}}{\cdot}{\Psi_4} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \AXC{$\tau_5\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_5}}{\cdot}{\Psi_5} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \RightLabel{$L\lor$} \BIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_1,\, \underline{D},\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_1,\, \underline{D},\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \RightLabel{$L\supset$} \BIC{$\tau_2\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_1,\,\underline{B},\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_1,\,\underline{B},\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \DP \qquad \begin{minipage}{10em} $\Psi_4\,=\; p,\,q_1,\,r_1,\,C$ \\[1ex] $\Psi_5\,=\; p,\,q_1,\,r_2,\,C$ \end{minipage}$$ For the critical sequent $\tau_4$, we have 3 possible options: 1. Apply rule $L\supset$ with main formula $C$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_4}}{\cdot}{\Psi_4} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2}$. 2. Apply rule $R\lor_1$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_4}}{\cdot}{\Psi_4} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1}$. 3. Apply rule $R\lor_2$; by [\[search:5\]](#search:5), this requires $\mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_4}}{\cdot}{\Psi_4} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2}$. We have $$\begin{array}{l} \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_4}}{\cdot}{\Psi_4} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:3}}$)} \qquad \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_4}}{\cdot}{\Psi_4} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2} \quad\mbox{(see $\sigma_{\eqref{exE:5}}$)} \qquad \mathtt{D}^{\ast}_{E}\mbox{$\,\not\rhd\,$} \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi_4}}{\cdot}{\Psi_4} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1} \end{array}$$ Thus, we select [\[exE:choice11\]](#exE:choice11) and we get $$\AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_1,\,r_1,\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_1,\,r_1,\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1} $} \RightLabel{$R\lor_1$} \UIC{$\tau_4\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_1,\,r_1,\,C }}{\cdot}{p,\,q_1,\,r_1,\,C } \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \DP$$ The $\mathbf{Gbu}(E)$-derivations of the sequents $\tau_5$ and $\tau_3$ have a similar construction: $$\begin{array}{c} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_1,\,r_2,\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_1,\,r_2,\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2} $} \RightLabel{$R\lor_2$} \UIC{$\tau_5\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_1,\,r_2,\,C }}{\cdot}{p,\,q_1,\,r_2,\,C } \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \DP \\[6ex] \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,C}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,C} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} $} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,r_1}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,r_1} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_1}}{\cdot}{r_1} $} \RightLabel{$R\lor_1$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,r_1}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,r_1} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \AXC{} \RightLabel{$\mathrm{Ax}$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,r_2}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,r_2} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{r_2}}{\cdot}{r_2} $} \RightLabel{$R\lor_2$} \UIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,r_2 }}{\cdot}{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,r_2 } \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \RightLabel{$L\lor$} \BIC{$ \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_2,\, B,\,\underline{D}}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_2,\, B,\,\underline{D}} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \RightLabel{$L\supset$} \BIC{$\tau_3\;=\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,\underline{C}}}{\cdot}{p,\,q_2,\,B,\,\underline{C}} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{D}}{\cdot}{D} $} \DP \end{array}$$ and this completes the definition of the $\mathbf{Gbu}(E)$-derivation of $E$. $\Diamond$

### Lemma 9
`lemma:gbuInv`  ·  p.30

Let $G$ be a formula, let $\mathtt{D}_{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$, $\Psi\subseteq {\normalfont\textsc{Sl}}(G)$ and $\Omega\subseteq {\overline\Gamma}$. 1. If $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{A,B,\Psi}}{\cdot}{A,B,\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{A\land B,\Psi}}{\cdot}{A\land B,\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$. 2. If $C_1\land C_2\in{\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(G)$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi}}{\cdot}{\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_k}}{\cdot}{C_k}$ with $k\in\{1,2\}$ then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi}}{\cdot}{\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_1\land C_2}}{\cdot}{C_1\land C_2}$. 3. If $A_1\lor A_2\in{\normalfont\textsc{Sl}}(G)$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{A_k,\Psi}}{\cdot}{A_k,\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$ with $k\in\{1,2\}$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{A_1\lor A_2,\Psi}}{\cdot}{A_1\lor A_2,\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$. 4. If $A\supset B\in{\normalfont\textsc{Sl}}(G)$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{B,\Psi}}{\cdot}{B,\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{A\supset B,\Psi}}{\cdot}{A\supset B,\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$. 5. If $A\supset B\in{\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(G)$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi}}{\cdot}{\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B}$, with $A\in\mathcal{C}l(\Psi)$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi}}{\cdot}{\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{A\supset B}}{\cdot}{A\supset B}$. 6. If $A\supset B\in{\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(G)$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{A,\Psi}}{\cdot}{A,\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B}$ with $A\not\in\mathcal{C}l(\Psi)$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Psi}}{\cdot}{\Psi} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{A\supset B}}{\cdot}{A\supset B}$. 7. If $C_1\land C_2\in{\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(G)$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_k}}{\cdot}{C_k}$ with $k\in\{1,2\}$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_1\land C_2}}{\cdot}{C_1\land C_2}$. 8. If $A\supset B\in{\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(G)$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B}$ with $A\in\mathcal{C}l(\Omega)$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{A\supset B}}{\cdot}{A\supset B}$. 9. If $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{A,\Omega}}{\cdot}{A,\Omega} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B}$ with $A\not\in\mathcal{C}l(\Omega)$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{A\supset B}}{\cdot}{A\supset B}$.

### Lemma 10
`lemma:gbuiOr`  ·  p.32

Let $G$ be a formula, let $\mathtt{D}_{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$ and $\Omega \subseteq {\overline\Gamma}$. If $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_1}}{\cdot}{C_1}$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_2}}{\cdot}{C_2}$, then $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_1\lor C_2}}{\cdot}{C_1\lor C_2}$.

### Lemma 11
`lemma:gbuSuccAt`  ·  p.32

Let $G$ be a formula and let $\mathtt{D}_{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$. Let $\tau= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{F}}{\cdot}{F}$ be such that $\Omega\subseteq {\overline\Gamma}$ and $F\in\mbox{$\mathcal{V}$}^\bot$, and let us assume that: 1. $F\not\in\Omega$; 2. for every $A\supset B\in\Omega$, $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{A}}{\cdot}{A}$. Then, $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd\tau$.

### Lemma 12
`lemma:gbuSuccOr`  ·  p.33

Let $G$ be a formula and let $\mathtt{D}_{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$. Let $\tau= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \Rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_1\lor C_2}}{\cdot}{C_1\lor C_2}$ be such that $\Omega\subseteq {\overline\Gamma}$, and let us assume that: 1. for every $A\supset B\in\Omega$, $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{A}}{\cdot}{A}$. 2. $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_1}}{\cdot}{C_1}$ and $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Omega}}{\cdot}{\Omega} \rightarrow_g\ifthenelse{\isempty{C_2}}{\cdot}{C_2}$. Then, $\mathtt{D}_{G}\rhd\tau$. 

### Theorem 8 (Correctness of BSearch)
`theo:search`  ·  p.33

Let $G$ be a formula, let $\tau$ be a $\mathbf{Gbu}(G)$-sequent and let $\mathtt{D}_{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$ satisfying [\[search:ass1\]](#search:ass1) and [\[search:ass2\]](#search:ass2). Then, $\mbox{\sc BSearch}(\tau,\mathtt{D}_{G})$ computes a $\mathbf{Gbu}(G)$-derivation of $\tau$.

### Theorem 9
`theo:GBU-FRJ`  ·  p.34

$\vdash_{\mathbf{Gbu}(G)} G$ iff ${\not\vdash}_{\mathbf{FRJ}(G)} G$.

### Theorem 10 (Completeness of FRJ(G) and Gbu(G))

1. $G\not\in\mathrm{IPL}$ implies $\vdash_{\mathbf{FRJ}(G)} G$. 2. $G\in\mathrm{IPL}$ implies $\vdash_{\mathbf{Gbu}(G)} G$.

### Lemma 13
`lemma:rnk`  ·  p.36

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation of $G$. Then, $\mathrm{Rn}(\mathcal{D})=\mathrm{h}(\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D}))$. 

### Lemma 14
`lemma:minMod`  ·  p.36

Let $\mathcal{K}=\langle P,\leq,\rho, V \rangle$ be a countermodel for $G$, let $\alpha\in P$ and $C\in\Omega_\alpha$. - There exists an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation $\mathcal{D}^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)$ of $\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C) = \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Sigma}}{\cdot}{\Sigma} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta}}{\cdot}{\Theta} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$ such that: 1. $\mathrm{Rn}( \mathcal{D}^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C) ) \,<\, \mathrm{h}(\alpha)$; 2. $\Sigma\,\subseteq\, \Lambda^*_\alpha\, \subseteq \,\Sigma\cup\Theta$. - There exists an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation $\mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)$ of $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Gamma}}{\cdot}{\Gamma} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$ such that: 1. $\mathrm{Rn}( \mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C) )\,\leq\,\mathrm{h}(\alpha)$; 2. there is $\beta\in P$ such that $\alpha\leq \beta$ and $\Lambda^*_\beta\,\subseteq\, \Gamma$. 

### Theorem 11
`theo:minMod`  ·  p.36

Let $G\not\in \mathrm{IPL}$. Then, there exists an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation $\tilde\mathcal{D}$ of $G$ such that $\mathrm{h}(\mathrm{Mod}(\tilde\mathcal{D}))=\mathrm{h}(G)$. 

### Example 9
`ex:STMinH`  ·  p.37

Let $S$ be the instance of Scott Principle in Ex. [\[ex:frjNishimura\]](#ex:frjNishimura): $$\begin{array}{l} S \;= \; H\,\supset\, \neg\neg p \lor \neg p \qquad H\;=\; (\neg\neg p\supset p)\, \supset\, \neg p\lor p \\[1ex] {\normalfont\textsc{Sl}}(S) \:=\: \{\: H,\:\neg p\lor p,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p,\:p\:\} \\[.5ex] {\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(S) \:=\: \{\: S,\:\neg\neg p\lor \neg p,\:\neg\neg p \supset p,\: \neg\neg p,\:\neg p,\: p,\: \bot \:\} \end{array}$$ We have $\mathrm{h}(S)=2$. Let us consider the countermodel $\mathcal{K}_S$ for $S$ having height 2 depicted below, consisting of the worlds $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of height 0, the world $\gamma$ of height 1 and the root $\rho$ of height 2: ::: center ::: We define the sequents $\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)$ and $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)$ matching Lemma [\[lemma:minMod\]](#lemma:minMod). For each sequent $\sigma$, we display the rule applied to obtain $\sigma$ and the rank of $\sigma$. Using these annotations, one can immediately build the derivations $\mathcal{D}^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)$ and $\mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)$. We traverse the model $\mathcal{K}$ downwards, starting from the world $\alpha$ of height 0. We have: $$\Lambda^*_\alpha\,=\,\{\:\neg p\:\} \qquad \Lambda_\alpha\;=\;\Lambda^*_\alpha\:\cup\:\{\:\neg p\lor p,\:H\:\} \qquad \Omega_\alpha\;=\;\{\:\bot,\:p,\:\neg\neg p\:\}$$ Note that $H\not\in\Lambda^*_\alpha$ since $\alpha\Vdash\neg\neg p \supset p$. Firstly, we define all the sequents $\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)$, where $C\in \Omega_\alpha$; formulas $C$ are considered in increasing order of size. $$\begin{array}{lrl|l|l} \mbox{Sequent}&&&\mbox{Applied rule}&\mbox{Rank}\\[.5ex] \hline &&&&\\[-1.5ex] \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\bot) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\:H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p}}{\cdot}{p,\:H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\bot}}{\cdot}{\bot} \qquad & \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow&-1 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(p) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p}}{\cdot}{H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} & \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow&-1 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\neg \neg p) \qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\:H,\:\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{p,\:H,\:\neg\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg \neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg \neg p} \qquad & \supset_\in\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\bot) \qquad &-1 \end{array}$$ Secondly, we define the sequents $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(C)$, where $C\in \Omega_\alpha$. $$\begin{array}{lrlll} \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\bot) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\bot}}{\cdot}{\bot} & \Join^{\mathrm{At}}\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(p)\qquad & 0 \\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(p) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} & \Join^{\mathrm{At}}\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(p) & 0 \\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\neg\neg p) \qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg\neg p} \qquad & \supset_\in\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\bot) & 0 \end{array}$$ Let us consider the world $\beta$ of height 0. We have: $$\Lambda^*_\beta\,=\,\{\:p,\:\neg\neg p\:\} \qquad \Lambda_\beta\,=\,\Lambda^*_\beta\:\cup\:\{\:\neg p\lor p,\:H\:\} \qquad \Omega_\beta\,=\,\{\:\bot,\:\neg p\:\}$$ For $C\in\Omega_\beta$, we define the sequents $\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\beta}(C)$: $$\begin{array}{lrlll} \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\beta}(\bot)\qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\:H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p}}{\cdot}{p,\:H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\bot}}{\cdot}{\bot} \qquad & \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow\qquad & -1 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\beta}(\neg p) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p}}{\cdot}{H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} & \supset_\in\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\beta}(\bot) &-1 \end{array}$$ For $C\in\Omega_\beta$, sequents $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(C)$ are: $$\begin{array}{lrlll} \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(\bot)\qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\:\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{p,\:\neg\neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\bot}}{\cdot}{\bot} \qquad& \Join^{\mathrm{At}}\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\beta}(\neg p)\qquad & 0 \\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(\neg p) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\:\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{p,\:\neg\neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} & \supset_\in\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(\bot) & 0 \end{array}$$ Let us consider $\gamma$, the only world of height 1. We have: $$\Lambda^*_\gamma\;=\;\Lambda_\gamma\;=\;\{\,H,\,\neg \neg p\,\} \qquad \Omega_\gamma\;=\;\{\,\bot,\,p,\,\neg p,\,\neg\neg p\supset p\,\}$$ For $C\in\Omega_\gamma$, sequents $\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(C)$ are: $$\begin{array}{lrlll} \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\bot) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\:H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p}}{\cdot}{p,\:H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\bot}}{\cdot}{\bot} \qquad & \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow&-1 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(p)& \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p}}{\cdot}{H,\:\neg\neg p,\:\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} & \mathrm{Ax}_\rightarrow&-1 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg p) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{H,\:\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{H,\:\neg\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} & \supset_{\not\in}\;\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(\bot)\qquad & 0 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg \neg p\supset p) \qquad& \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg\neg p} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{H,\:\neg p}}{\cdot}{H,\:\neg p} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg \neg p\supset p}}{\cdot}{\neg \neg p\supset p} \qquad & \supset_\in\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(p) & -1 \end{array}$$ For $C\in \Omega_\gamma$, sequents $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\gamma}(C)$ are: $$\begin{array}{lrlll} \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\bot) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\:\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{p,\:\neg\neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\bot}}{\cdot}{\bot} \qquad& \Join^{\mathrm{At}}\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\beta}(\neg p)\qquad & 0 \\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\gamma}(p)\qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{H,\:\neg \neg p}}{\cdot}{H,\:\neg \neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p}}{\cdot}{p} \qquad & \Join^{\mathrm{At}}\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg p)\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg \neg p\supset p) \quad& 1 \\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg p)\qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p,\:\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{p,\:\neg\neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg p} & \supset_\in\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(\bot) & 0 \\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg\neg p \supset p)\qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{H,\:\neg \neg p}}{\cdot}{H,\:\neg \neg p} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg\neg p\supset p}}{\cdot}{\neg\neg p\supset p} \qquad& \supset_\in\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\gamma}(p) & 1 \end{array}$$ Finally, let us consider the root $\rho$ having height 2. We have: $$\Lambda^*_\rho=\Lambda_\rho=\{H\} \qquad \Omega_\rho ={\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(S)$$ We can inherit the following definitions from the worlds $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$: $$\begin{array}{l} \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\bot) \;=\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\bot) \qquad \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(p) \;=\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(p) \qquad \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg p) \,=\,\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg p) \\[.5ex] \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(\bot) \;=\;\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(\bot) \qquad \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(p) \,=\,\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(p) \qquad \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg p) \;=\;\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(\neg p) \\[.5ex] \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg \neg p) \;=\;\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\neg \neg p) \qquad \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg \neg p \supset p) \,=\,\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg \neg p\supset p) \end{array}$$ For $C\in\{\,\neg\neg p,\,\neg\neg p\supset p,\, \neg\neg p\lor \neg p,\, S \,\}$, the sequents $\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(C)$ are: $$\begin{array}{lrllll} \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg\neg p} & \supset_{\not\in}\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(\bot) & 0 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p\supset p) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg\neg p \supset p}}{\cdot}{\neg\neg p \supset p} & \supset_{\not\in}\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\gamma}(p) & 1 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p\lor \neg p) \qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg\neg p \lor\neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg\neg p \lor\neg p} \qquad & \lor\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p)\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg p) \quad & 0 \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(S) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{S}}{\cdot}{S} & \supset_\in\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p\lor \neg p) & 0 \end{array}$$ For $C\in\{\,\neg\neg p\lor \neg p,\, S \,\}$, the sequents $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(C)$ are: $$\begin{array}{lrlll} \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p\lor \neg p)\qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{\neg\neg p \lor \neg p}}{\cdot}{\neg\neg p \lor \neg p} \qquad & \Join^\lor\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p\supset p) \;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p)\;\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\gamma}(\neg p) \quad & 2 \\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(S) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{H}}{\cdot}{H} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{S}}{\cdot}{S} & \supset_\in\;\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(\neg\neg p\lor \neg p) & 2 \end{array}$$ The $\mathbf{FRJ}(S)$-derivation $\mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(S)$ of $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(S)$ obtained in the end is an $\mathbf{FRJ}(S)$-derivation of the goal $S$. Note that $\mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(S)$ essentially coincides with the derivation in Fig. [\[fig:frjST\]](#fig:frjST), hence the model $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(S))$ extracted from $\mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(S)$ is isomorphic to the countermodel $\mathcal{K}_S$ displayed at the beginning of this example. $\Diamond$

### Example 10
`ex:DUMnonMIN`  ·  p.39

Let $C$ be the formula $$\begin{array}{l} C \;= \; A\lor B \qquad A\;=\; (p_1\supset p_2)\lor (p_2\supset p_1) \qquad B\;=\; (q_1\supset q_2)\lor (q_2\supset q_1) \end{array}$$ We have $\mathrm{h}(C)=1$. Let $\mathcal{K}_C$ be the following countermodel for $C$ of height 1, consisting of the worlds $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of height 0 and of the root $\rho$ of height 1: ::: center ::: One can easily check that there is no countermodel for $C$ having less than 3 worlds, hence $\mathcal{K}_C$ is a minimal countermodel for $C$. We have: $$\begin{array}{l} {\normalfont\textsc{Sl}}(C) \;=\; \{\: p_1,\:p_2,\:q_1,\:q_2 \:\} \\[1ex] {\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(C) \:=\: \{\: C,\:A,\:B,\: p_1\supset p_2,\;p_2\supset p_1,\:q_1\supset q_2,\;q_2\supset q_1,\; p_1,\:p_2,\:q_1,\:q_2 \:\} \\[1ex] \Lambda^*_\alpha\;=\;\Lambda_\alpha\;=\;\{\:p_1,\:q_1\:\} \qquad \Omega_\alpha\;=\;\{\:\:p_2,\: q_2,\: p_1\supset p_2,\:q_1\supset q_2 \:\} \\[1ex] \Lambda^*_\beta\;=\;\Lambda_\beta\;=\;\{\:p_2,\:q_2\:\} \qquad \Omega_\beta\;=\;\{\: \:p_1,\: q_1,\;p_2\supset p_1,\:q_2\supset q_1\:\} \\[1ex] \Lambda^*_\rho\;=\;\Lambda_\rho\;=\;\emptyset \qquad \Omega_\rho \;=\;{\normalfont\textsc{Sr}}(C) \end{array}$$ We define the sequents $\sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\delta}(C)$ and $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\delta}(C)$, where $\delta\in\{\alpha,\beta,\rho\}$ and $C\in\Omega_\delta$, only showing the sequents needed to prove the goal. $$\begin{array}{lrlll} \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(p_2) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1,\:q_1,\:q_2}}{\cdot}{p_1,\:q_1,\:q_2} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_2}}{\cdot}{p_2} & \mathrm{Ax}_\Rightarrow\\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(q_2) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1,\:p_2,\:q_1}}{\cdot}{p_1,\:p_2,\:q_1} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2}}{\cdot}{q_2} & \mathrm{Ax}_\Rightarrow\\ \hline \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(p_1) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_2,\:q_1,\:q_2}}{\cdot}{p_2,\:q_1,\:q_2} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1}}{\cdot}{p_1} & \mathrm{Ax}_\Rightarrow\\ \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(q_1) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1,\:p_2,\:q_2}}{\cdot}{p_1,\:p_2,\:q_2} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1}}{\cdot}{q_1} & \mathrm{Ax}_\Rightarrow\\ \hline \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(p_1 \supset p_2)\qquad & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1,\:q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1,\:q_2} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1\supset p_2}}{\cdot}{p_1\supset p_2} \qquad & \supset_{\not\in}\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(p_2) \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(p_2 \supset p_1) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1,\:q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1,\:q_2} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_2\supset p_1}}{\cdot}{p_2\supset p_1} & \supset_{\not\in}\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(p_1) \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(q_1 \supset q_2) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1,\:p_2}}{\cdot}{p_1,\:p_2} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1\supset q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1\supset q_2} & \supset_{\not\in}\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\alpha}(q_2) \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(q_2 \supset q_1) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1,\:p_2}}{\cdot}{p_1,\:p_2} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_2\supset q_1}}{\cdot}{q_2\supset q_1} & \supset_{\not\in}\; \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\beta}(q_1) \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(A) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{q_1,\:q_2}}{\cdot}{q_1,\:q_2} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{A}}{\cdot}{A} & \lor\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(p_1\supset p_2) \; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(p_2\supset p_1) \\ \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(B) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} \:;\: \ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1,\:p_2}}{\cdot}{p_1,\:p_2} & \; \rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{B}}{\cdot}{B} & \lor\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(q_1\supset q_2) \; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(q_2\supset q_1) \\ \hline \sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(C) & \ifthenelse{\isempty{}}{\cdot}{} &\;\Rightarrow\; \ifthenelse{\isempty{A\lor B}}{\cdot}{A\lor B} & \Join^\lor\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(A)\; \sigma^{\rightarrow}_{\rho}(B) \end{array}$$ The goal $C$ is proved by the $\mathbf{FRJ}(C)$-derivation $\mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(C)$ of $\sigma^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(C)$. The model $\mathrm{Mod}( \mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(C) )$ extracted from $\mathcal{D}^{\Rightarrow}_{\rho}(C)$ is: ::: center ::: Such a model has the minimal height 1, as expected, but it is not minimal. To obtain minimal models, we should redesign $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$ in a multi-succedent style, so that axioms of the kind $\ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1,q_1}}{\cdot}{p_1,q_1} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p_2,q_2}}{\cdot}{p_2,q_2}$ and $\ifthenelse{\isempty{p_2,q_2}}{\cdot}{p_2,q_2} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{p_1,q_1}}{\cdot}{p_1,q_1}$ are allowed. Thus, we should have regular axioms of the kind $\ifthenelse{\isempty{\Gamma^{\mathrm{At}}}}{\cdot}{\Gamma^{\mathrm{At}}} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{\Delta^{\mathrm{At}}}}{\cdot}{\Delta^{\mathrm{At}}}$, where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{At}}$ and $\Delta^{\mathrm{At}}$ are disjoint sets of propositional variables such that $\Gamma^{\mathrm{At}}\subseteq\mathrm{Lhs}(G)$ and $\Delta^{\mathrm{At}}\subseteq\mathrm{Rhs}(G)$. However, this would cause an exponential blow-up of the number of provable sequents and proof-search would become unfeasible. E.g., in this case we would get 64 regular axioms instead of 5. $\Diamond$

### Lemma 15
`lemma:closure`  ·  p.40

Let $\mathcal{K}$ be a countermodel for $G$ and $\alpha$ a world of $\mathcal{K}$. Then, $\Lambda_\alpha=\mathcal{C}l(\Lambda_\alpha)=\mathcal{C}l(\Lambda^*_\alpha)$.

### Lemma 16 (aka Lemma 3.9 of Sec.3)
`app:lemma:soundFRJ`  ·  p.51  ·  **appendix**

Let $\mathcal{D}$ be an $\mathbf{FRJ}(G)$-derivation of $G$, let $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal{D})$ be the model extracted from $\mathcal{D}$ and $\phi$ the map associated with $\mathcal{D}$. For every sequent $\sigma$ occurring in $\mathcal{D}$: 1. if $\sigma= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Gamma}}{\cdot}{\Gamma} \Rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$, then $\phi(\sigma)\Vdash\Gamma$ and $\phi(\sigma) \nVdash C$; 2. if $\sigma= \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Sigma}}{\cdot}{\Sigma} \,;\, \ifthenelse{\isempty{\Theta}}{\cdot}{\Theta} \rightarrow\ifthenelse{\isempty{C}}{\cdot}{C}$, let $\sigma_p\in\mathrm{P}(\mathcal{D})$ such that $\sigma\mapsto\sigma_p$ and $\sigma_p\Vdash\Sigma\cap\mathrm{Sf}^-(C)$; then $\sigma_p\nVdash C$.

### Lemma 17
`lemma:soundnessProperties`  ·  p.53  ·  **appendix**

Soundness properties [\[prop:soundr\]](#prop:soundr) and [\[prop:soundi\]](#prop:soundi) hold.

**Example 1** · `ex:impPS1`

```tex
Let $\s_1=\seqfrji{}{p,q}{B}$ be an $\FRJof{G}$-sequent such that the formula $p\lor q\imp B$ belongs to $\Sfr{G}$. To apply rule $\ruleIMPi$ to $\s_1$ so to get a sequent with $p\lor q\imp B$ in the right, we have to select a subset $\Lambda$ of $\{p,q\}$ satisfying the side condition $p\lor q\in\Clo{\Lambda}$. The following three choices are possible: \[ \begin{array}{lll} \Lambda_1\;=\;\{p\} & \Lambda_2\;=\;\{q\} & \Lambda_3\;=\;\{p,q\} \\[1.5ex] \AXC{$\seqfrji{}{p,q}{B}$} \RightLabel{$\ruleIMPi$} \UIC{$\seqfrji{p}{q}{p\lor q\imp B}$} \DP \hspace{2em} & \AXC{$\seqfrji{}{p,q}{B}$} \RightLabel{$\ruleIMPi$} \UIC{$\seqfrji{q}{p}{p\lor q\imp B}$} \DP \hspace{2em} & \AXC{$\seqfrji{}{p,q}{B}$} \RightLabel{$\ruleIMPi$} \UIC{$\seqfrji{p,q}{}{p\lor q\imp B}$} \DP \end{array} \] We point out that $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are minimal sets satisfying the side condition, while $\Lambda_3$ is not. Indeed, the empty set is the only proper subset of $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ and $p\lor q\not\in\Clo{\emptyset}$. On the other hand, $\Lambda_3$ is not minimal, since both $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$ are proper subsets of $\Lambda_3$. \EndEs
```

**Example 3**

```tex
Let $\s_1=\seqfrji{\Sigma_1 }{\Theta_1}{B}$, where $\Sigma_1=\{B\imp X_1, B\imp X_2, C\imp X_3 \}$ and $C\neq B$. We cannot apply a join rule having $\s_1$ as only premise since the formula $C\imp X_3$ would not be supported (while both $B\imp X_1$ and $B\imp X_2$ are, being $B$ the right formula of $\s_1$). Thus, to apply a join rule, we need a further premise $\s_2=\seqfrji{\Sigma_2}{\Theta_2}{C}$ such that $\Sigma_1\subseteq\Sigma_2\cup\Theta_2$ and $\Sigma_2\subseteq\Sigma_1\cup\Theta_1$ (see~\ref{sc:J1}). In turn, $\Sigma_2$ might contain some non-supported formulas; e.g., a formula $D\imp X_4$ such that $D\neq B$ and $D\neq C$; in this case, we need a further premise $\s_3$ s.t. $\Rhs{\s_3}=D$ to support it. \EndEs
```


**Lemma 2** · `lemma:soundFRJ`

```tex
Let $\Dcal$ be an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation of $G$, let $\Mod{\Dcal}$ be the model extracted from $\Dcal$ and $\phi$ the map associated with $\Dcal$. For every sequent $\s$ occurring in $\Dcal$: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),ref=(\roman*)] \item if $\s= \seqfrj{\G}{C}$, then $\phi(\s)\forcing\G$ and $\phi(\s) \nforcing C$; \item if $\s= \seqfrji{\Sigma}{\Theta}{C}$, let $\s_p\in\PS{\Dcal}$ such that~$\s\mapsto\s_p$ and $\s_p\forcing\Sigma\cap\Sfm{C}$; then $\s_p\nforcing C$.\qed \end{enumerate}
```

**Theorem 2** · `theo:soundFRJ`

```tex
Let $\Dcal$ be an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation of $G$. Then, $\Mod{\Dcal}$ is a countermodel for $G$.
```

**Lemma 3** · `lemma:wg`

```tex
$\s_1\mapsto \s_2$ implies $\stru{0,0,0}\preceq \wg{\s_2} \prec \wg{\s_1}$. \qed
```

**Lemma 4** · `lemma:branch`

```tex
Let $\Dcal$ be an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation, let $\Bcal$ be a branch of $\Dcal$ and $N=\size{G}$. Then: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)] \item the length of the branch $\Bcal$ is $O(N^2)$; \item $\Bcal$ contains $N$ p-sequents at most. \end{enumerate}
```

**Theorem 3** · `theo:height`

```tex
Let $\Dcal$ be an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation and $N=\size{G}$. Then: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)] \item $\height{\Dcal}\,=\,O(N^2)$. \item $\height{\Mod{\Dcal}}\,\leq\, N$. \qed \end{enumerate}
```

**Lemma 5** · `lemma:subsRules`

```tex
Let \[ \AXC{$\s_1 \;\cdots\; \s_n$} \RightLabel{$\Rcal$} \UIC{$\s$} \DP \] be an instance of a rule of $\FRJof{G}$ and let $\s_1\sqsubseteq \s'_1$, \dots, $\s_n\sqsubseteq \s'_n$. Then, \[ \AXC{$\s'_1 \;\cdots\; \s'_n$} \RightLabel{$\Rcal$} \UIC{$\s'$} \DP \] is an instance of $\Rcal$ in $\FRJof{G}$ where $\s\sqsubseteq \s'$.
```

**Theorem 4** · `theo:fsearchAdequate`

```tex
$\FSearch$ is an adequate proof-search procedure.
```

**Lemma 6** · `lemma:compactSatDB`

```tex
Let $G$ be a formula and let $\DBof{G}^1$ be a compact saturated database for $G$. For every saturated database $\DBof{G}^2$ for $G$, $\DBof{G}^1\subseteq \DBof{G}^2$.
```

**Theorem 5** · `theo:uniquetSatDB`

```tex
For every formula $G$, there exists a unique compact saturated database $\DBMof{G}$ for $G$, which is the minimum saturated database for $G$.
```

```tex
If $\proves{\GBUof{G}} \tau$, then $\tau$ is valid.\qed
```

```tex
$\proves{\GBUof{G}} G$ implies $G\in\IPL$. \qed
```

```tex
Let $G$ be a formula, let $\DBof{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$ and $\Omega \subseteq \bG$. If $\DBof{G}\eval\seqgbui{\Omega}{C_1}$ and $\DBof{G}\eval\seqgbui{\Omega}{C_2}$, then $\DBof{G}\eval\seqgbui{\Omega}{C_1\lor C_2}$.
```

**Lemma 11** · `lemma:gbuSuccAt`

```tex
Let $G$ be a formula and let $\DBof{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$. Let $\tau=\seqgbu{\Omega}{F}$ be such that $\Omega\subseteq \bG$ and $F\in\Prime$, and let us assume that: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),ref=(\roman*)] \item $F\not\in\Omega$; \item for every $A\imp B\in\Omega$,\ $\DBof{G}\eval\seqgbui{\Omega}{A}$. \end{enumerate} Then, $\DBof{G}\eval \tau$.
```

**Lemma 12** · `lemma:gbuSuccOr`

```tex
Let $G$ be a formula and let $\DBof{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$. Let $\tau=\seqgbu{\Omega}{C_1\lor C_2}$ be such that $\Omega\subseteq \bG$, and let us assume that: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),ref=(\roman*)] \item for every $A\imp B\in\Omega$,\ $\DBof{G}\eval\seqgbui{\Omega}{A}$. \item $\DBof{G}\eval\seqgbui{\Omega}{C_1}$ and $\DBof{G}\eval\seqgbui{\Omega}{C_2}$. \end{enumerate} Then, $\DBof{G}\eval \tau$. \qed
```

**Theorem 8** · `theo:search`

```tex
Let $G$ be a formula, let $\tau$ be a $\GBUof{G}$-sequent and let $\DBof{G}$ be a saturated database for $G$ satisfying~\ref{search:ass1} and~\ref{search:ass2}. Then, $\Search(\tau,\DBof{G})$ computes a $\GBUof{G}$-derivation of $\tau$.
```

**Theorem 9** · `theo:GBU-FRJ`


**Theorem 10**

```tex

```

**Lemma 13** · `lemma:rnk`

```tex
Let $\Dcal$ be an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation of $G$. Then, $\Rn{\Dcal}=\height{\Mod{\Dcal}}$. \qed
```

**Lemma 14** · `lemma:minMod`

```tex
Let $\K=\stru{P,\leq,\rho, V}$ be a countermodel for $G$, let $\a\in P$ and $C\in\Omega_\a$. \begin{itemize} \item There exists an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation $\derfrji{\a}{C}$ of $\sigmairr{\a}{C} =\seqfrji{\Sigma}{\Theta}{C}$ such that: \begin{enumerate} [label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)] \item $\Rn{ \derfrji{\a}{C} } \,<\, \height{\a}$; \item $\Sigma\,\subseteq\, \Lambdas_\a \, \subseteq \,\Sigma\cup\Theta$. \end{enumerate} \item There exists an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation $\derfrjr{\a}{C}$ of $\sigmareg{\a}{C}=\seqfrj{\G}{C}$ such that: \begin{enumerate} [start=3, label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)] \item $\Rn{ \derfrjr{\a}{C} }\,\leq\,\height{\a}$; \item there is $\b\in P$ such that $\a\leq \b$ and $\Lambdas_\b\,\subseteq\, \G$. \qed \end{enumerate} \end{itemize}
```

**Theorem 11** · `theo:minMod`

```tex
Let $G\not\in \IPL$. Then, there exists an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation $\tilde\Dcal$ of $G$ such that $\height{\Mod{\tilde\Dcal}}=\height{G}$. \qed
```

**Lemma 15** · `lemma:closure`

```tex
Let $\K$ be a countermodel for $G$ and $\a$ a world of $\K$. Then, $\Lambda_\a=\Clo{\Lambda_\a}=\Clo{\Lambdas_\a}$.
```

**Lemma 16** · `app:lemma:soundFRJ`

```tex
Let $\Dcal$ be an $\FRJof{G}$-derivation of $G$, let $\Mod{\Dcal}$ be the model extracted from $\Dcal$ and $\phi$ the map associated with $\Dcal$. For every sequent $\s$ occurring in $\Dcal$: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),ref=(\roman*)] \item if $\s= \seqfrj{\G}{C}$, then $\phi(\s)\forcing\G$ and $\phi(\s) \nforcing C$; \item if $\s= \seqfrji{\Sigma}{\Theta}{C}$, let $\s_p\in\PS{\Dcal}$ such that~$\s\mapsto\s_p$ and $\s_p\forcing\Sigma\cap\Sfm{C}$; then $\s_p\nforcing C$. \end{enumerate}
```

**Lemma 17** · `lemma:soundnessProperties`

```tex
Soundness properties~\ref{prop:soundr} and~\ref{prop:soundi} hold.
```
